title: Enlarge buffer cache and align planner I/O costs to cut GetUserTweets terminal occupancy
configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is far below the 2TB host RAM, so the tweets working set is not retained; low_buffer_hit_ratio is active and DataFileRead/BufferIO waits appear. effective_cache_size=524288 (4GB) and random_page_cost=4.0/seq_page_cost=1.0 make the planner overprice cached random index reads, so GetUserTweets (88.5% of terminal capacity, p50 196us) pays repeated physical I/O.
mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates finite client terminal time (0.885 fraction). With only 128MB shared_buffers the hot tweets pages are evicted, producing DataFileRead and BufferIO waits and inflating per-call latency. Raising shared_buffers to 1GB retains the working set; raising effective_cache_size to 8GB and lowering random_page_cost to 1.5 with seq_page_cost 0.9 makes the planner correctly value cached index scans and prefer them over costlier alternatives, and effective_io_concurrency=8 enables prefetch. Together these reduce physical reads per GetUserTweets call, lowering terminal occupancy and raising completed-transaction goodput.
query_effect: GetUserTweets index scans on tweets should hit shared_buffers more often, reducing DataFileRead/BufferIO waits and per-call latency; planner keeps Index Scan but with lower estimated cost for cached random access.
expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps above 20596 as GetUserTweets terminal occupancy falls.
expected_latency_effect: Decrease GetUserTweets p50/p95 latency and overall p95.

predictions.rationale: Larger buffer cache plus cache-aware planner costs reduce physical reads per dominant transaction.
Lower per-call latency for GetUserTweets frees terminal capacity.
Better cache retention reduces IO wait backends.
Reduced terminal occupancy converts to higher completed-transaction goodput.

alternatives.statement: If the dominant cost is WAL sync rather than buffer misses, the buffer bundle will not move GetUserTweets latency and WAL knobs (wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay) would be needed instead.
If the working set already fits and only planner costing is wrong, effective_cache_size/random_page_cost alone would help while shared_buffers change is neutral; io_waiting_backends would stay flat.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves 128MB shared_buffers against a 2TB host and prices random reads at 4.0, so the dominant GetUserTweets transaction repeatedly pays physical I/O. A coherent cache-capacity plus planner-cost bundle directly targets the diagnosed low_buffer_hit_ratio and terminal saturation.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 1GB = 131072*8kB, 8x current, well within safe 8192-65536... capped at 65536 (512MB) to stay in allowed high; use 65536.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: database cache capacity to retain hot tweets pages

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 8GB estimate, within 131072-1048576; reflects large host RAM for planner.
Modest prefetch depth within 0-256; 8 matches typical SSD queue depth.
Lower toward seq_page_cost to reflect cached random reads; within 1.0-6.0.
Slight reduction to keep ratio coherent; within 0.5-2.0.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost

cross_domain_requirements: WAL commit-path knobs (wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay, wal_compression) remain owned by memory_storage; not executed here.

edges.relation: raises cache hit ratio and lowers random-read cost
